Shared laws, commands and teaching applying to all within the stated audience or conditions. General does not remove covenant, historical, priestly or household limits. Read the existing Transformed, Fulfilled, Unchanged, Everlasting and other classifications alongside each entry.

Some source records still need their audience resolved. These are explicitly marked audience review pending; their provisional filing here is not a claim that they apply universally. Passage groups may contain both shared teaching and personal directions.

General · Personal · Instructions overview

3,869 study records in this view. Entries can overlap; this is not a count of distinct biblical commands. Ordered by the first source book, chapter and verse.

The source wording follows the Saints Greek-English text: the Septuagint for the Old Testament and the Greek New Testament. Headings and application notes are study summaries. Preserve the passage’s speaker, audience, conditions and grammatical form. Source alignment checked 6 November 2026; independent critical-Greek review remains in progress.

C0672 · Do not eat an animal that died of itself

Source wording · Saints Greek-English

22:8 He shall not eat an animal found dead or torn by beasts, becoming unclean through them. I am the Lord.

Leviticus 22:8

14:21 You shall not eat anything that dies of itself; it shall be given unto the resident alien within your cities, and he shall eat it, or you may sell it unto a foreigner; for you are a holy people unto the Lord your God. You shall not boil a lamb in its mother’s milk.

Deuteronomy 14:21

Audience: A shared rule for the people, office or circumstances specified in the source. Preserve its covenant, priestly, civil or ritual limits and the existing fulfillment classification.

Classification: Transformed · Torah requirement

Topic: Food, ritual purity and cleansing

Original scope: Christians differ about the reach of these passages. Acts 15:19–29 must also be read; the instruction concerning blood is treated separately.

Jesus locates defilement in the heart, and the apostolic writings address receiving food with thanksgiving and avoiding judgment over food. This catalogue reads the old food distinctions through those passages.

S095 · Firstfruits, the count and the Festival of Weeks

Source wording · Saints Greek-English

This is the cited study context; the record does not identify a separate primary command passage.

23:9 And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

23:10 Say unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: When you enter the land which I give unto you, and reap its harvest, you shall bring a sheaf as the first portion of your harvest unto the priest;

23:11 and he shall offer up the sheaf before the Lord, acceptable for you; the priest shall offer it up on the morrow after the first day.

23:12 And on the day you bring the sheaf, you shall offer an unblemished year-old sheep as a whole burnt offering unto the Lord.

23:13 And its sacrifice shall be two tenths of fine flour kneaded with oil, a sacrifice unto the Lord, a sweet savour unto the Lord. Its drink offering shall be a quarter of a hin of wine.

23:14 And you shall eat neither bread nor roasted fresh grain until that very day, until you bring the gifts to your God. This is an everlasting ordinance throughout your generations in every dwelling of yours.

23:15 And you shall count from the day after the Sabbath, from the day you bring the sheaf of the presentation, seven complete weeks.

23:16 Until the day after the last week you shall count fifty days, and then present a new sacrifice unto the Lord.

23:17 From your dwelling you shall bring bread as a presentation, two loaves. They shall be made from two tenths of fine flour and baked leavened, as firstfruits unto the Lord.

23:18 And with the loaves you shall bring seven unblemished year-old lambs, one calf from the herd, and two unblemished rams. They shall be a whole burnt offering unto the Lord, with their sacrifices and drink offerings, a sacrifice, a sweet savour unto the Lord.

23:19 And they shall offer one male young goat from the goats for sin and two year-old lambs as a sacrifice of deliverance with the firstfruits loaves.

23:20 And the priest shall present them with the firstfruits loaves as a presentation before the Lord, with the two lambs. They shall be holy unto the Lord; they shall belong unto the priest who presents them.

23:21 And you shall proclaim this day a convocation; it shall be holy for you. You shall do no laborious work on it. This is an everlasting ordinance throughout your generations in every dwelling of yours.

23:22 And when you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not finish the remainder of the harvest of your field when you reap; neither shall you gather what falls from your harvest; you shall leave them for the poor and for the resident foreigner; I am the Lord your God.

Leviticus 23:9–22

Audience: Shared instruction or study teaching. Read the original audience, conditions and existing classification before applying it.

Classification: Study context · Topical study

Topic: Sabbath, appointed times and remembrance

Original scope: Text and setting: Israel’s worship

Connection to Christ: Paul explicitly calls the risen Christ the firstfruits; Acts records the Spirit’s coming at Pentecost. This does not declare every festival detail completed. Christian response today: Live in resurrection hope and respond to the Spirit; keep firstfruits, the count and Weeks distinct in the Torah calendar.
